title: Article 356 — Provisions in case of failure of constitutional machinery in States

content.overview: Article 356 (President’s Rule) provides that if the President, on receipt of a report from the Governor of a State or otherwise, is satisfied that a situation has arisen in which the government of the State cannot be carried on in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution, the President may by Proclamation assume to himself all or any of the functions of the State Government and the powers of the Governor or any body/authority in the State other than the Legislature, declare that the powers of the State Legislature shall be exercisable by or under the authority of Parliament, and make incidental provisions. The Proclamation must be approved by Parliament and is subject to duration limits (generally 6 months at a time, with a maximum typically of 3 years subject to conditions). Judicial review applies (S.R. Bommai principles).
content.glance: President’s Rule: if State government cannot be carried on in accordance with the Constitution. President assumes State executive functions; Parliament may exercise State legislative powers. Parliamentary approval; judicial review (Bommai).
content.study:
Article 356:
**Trigger:** President satisfied (on Governor’s report or otherwise) that State government cannot be carried on in accordance with the Constitution.
**Consequences:** President may assume State executive functions and powers of Governor/other authorities (except the Legislature); declare that State Legislature powers are exercisable by or under authority of Parliament; make consequential provisions including suspension of constitutional provisions relating to State bodies.
**Approval & duration:** Proclamation laid before Parliament; ceases after 2 months unless approved; once approved, continues for 6 months at a time; maximum period subject to constitutional limits (including 3-year ceiling with conditions involving Election Commission certificate and National Emergency in certain extensions historically structured).
**Judicial review:** S.R. Bommai — satisfaction is justiciable on limited grounds; floor test preferred for majority disputes; dissolution of Assembly not automatic.

Examination: failure of constitutional machinery; Governor’s report or otherwise; assumption of functions; parliamentary role; Bommai safeguards; contrast Art 352.

sections.heading: Key elements
sections.body:
1. Satisfaction that State government cannot be carried on in accordance with the Constitution.
2. President may assume State executive functions; Parliament may exercise State legislative powers.
3. Parliamentary approval and periodic renewal; constitutional duration limits.
4. Judicial review of satisfaction and process (Bommai).

questionsAndAnswers.question: Explain President’s Rule under Article 356.
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 356, if the President, on receipt of a report from the Governor of a State or otherwise, is satisfied that a situation has arisen in which the government of the State cannot be carried on in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution, the President may by Proclamation assume to himself all or any of the functions of the Government of the State and the powers vested in or exercisable by the Governor or any body or authority in the State other than the Legislature of the State, and declare that the powers of the Legislature of the State shall be exercisable by or under the authority of Parliament. The Proclamation requires parliamentary approval and is subject to duration limits. The Supreme Court in S.R. Bommai held that the President’s satisfaction is justiciable on limited grounds and that majority should ordinarily be tested on the floor of the Assembly.
